# Problem

RFC 9457 problem-details object. The optional `code` field is a plexsphere extension that carries the machine-readable error taxonomy (RFC 8628 device-flow codes, federation_kind_mismatch, etc.). 

## Properties

Name | Type | Description | Notes
------------ | ------------- | ------------- | -------------
**type** | **str** | URI reference that identifies the problem type. | 
**title** | **str** | Short, human-readable summary of the problem. | 
**status** | **int** | HTTP status code generated for this occurrence. | 
**detail** | **str** | Human-readable explanation specific to this occurrence. The text is written for the caller and never carries persistence or infrastructure internals.  | 
**instance** | **str** | URI reference identifying the specific occurrence. | 
**correlation_id** | **str** | Correlation id pairing this problem with the server log record for the same failure. Echoed on the &#x60;X-Correlation-Id&#x60; response header.  | 
**code** | **str** | Optional machine-readable error code. Device-flow errors use the RFC 8628 taxonomy (&#x60;authorization_pending&#x60;, &#x60;slow_down&#x60;, &#x60;access_denied&#x60;, &#x60;expired_token&#x60;, &#x60;invalid_grant&#x60;); service token mismatches use &#x60;federation_kind_mismatch&#x60;. CSRF defence-in-depth adds three 403 codes scoped to state-changing cookie-authenticated &#x60;/v1/*&#x60; requests. Bearer-authenticated requests and &#x60;GET&#x60; / &#x60;HEAD&#x60; requests are exempt. The codes are:    * &#x60;csrf_token_mismatch&#x60; — 403, the &#x60;X-Plexsphere-CSRF&#x60;     header is absent, empty, or does not byte-match the     &#x60;plexsphere_csrf&#x60; cookie. The cookie is rotated on     sign-in and on sign-out so a leaked token cannot     outlive the session it was minted for.   * &#x60;csrf_origin_mismatch&#x60; — 403, the request carried an     &#x60;Origin&#x60; header that is not in the configured     allowlist AND did not advertise     &#x60;Sec-Fetch-Site: same-origin&#x60;.   * &#x60;csrf_origin_not_configured&#x60; — 403, the deployment     does not configure &#x60;PLEXSPHERE_CSRF_ALLOWED_ORIGINS&#x60;.     A misconfigured production deployment surfaces this     code on every cookie-authenticated mutation rather     than silently bypassing the CSRF check. Mirrors the &#x60;ListNodes&#x60; &#x60;cursor_binding_mismatch&#x60; on &#x60;/v1/nodes&#x60;.   * &#x60;invalid_cloud_provider_mode&#x60; — 400, a Cloud create or patch named &#x60;provider_bundle_id&#x60; together with &#x60;provider_packages&#x60; or &#x60;provider_config_api_version&#x60;, stated &#x60;provider_package_overrides&#x60; while the Cloud declares (or comes to declare) its packages inline, or supplied a &#x60;provider_bundle_id&#x60; that is not a canonical UUID string. The two provider-configuration modes are exclusive.   * &#x60;unknown_provider_bundle&#x60; — 400, a Cloud create or patch named a &#x60;provider_bundle_id&#x60; no provider bundle answers to.   * &#x60;provider_bundle_provider_mismatch&#x60; — 400, the named provider bundle serves a different &#x60;provider&#x60; than the Cloud referencing it, so its packages could not serve the Cloud&#39;s ProviderConfig.   * &#x60;provider_bundle_version_not_found&#x60; — 400, a Cloud create or patch named a &#x60;provider_bundle_version&#x60; the referenced provider bundle never published. Distinct from &#x60;unknown_provider_bundle&#x60;: the bundle is right and the version is not, so the operator picks another version. The versions the bundle did publish are readable at &#x60;GET /v1/provider-bundles/{id}/versions&#x60;.   * &#x60;provider_bundle_reference_moved&#x60; — 409, a &#x60;PatchCloud&#x60; body that names no provider bundle but depends on the one the Cloud references (only &#x60;provider_bundle_version&#x60;, or &#x60;provider_package_overrides&#x60;) was decided against the reference the Cloud held when the request was read, and a competing writer moved that reference — another bundle, or another pinned version of the same one — before the write. Nothing was written; re-read the Cloud and send the patch again.  The provider-bundle surface — the second aggregate of the Cloud Inventory sub-context — adds the closed taxonomy below. Each code maps to exactly one repo / service / adapter sentinel and one HTTP status:    * &#x60;invalid_catalog_source_id&#x60; — 400, path &#x60;{id}&#x60; on &#x60;/v1/blueprint-catalogs/{id}&#x60; was not a non-zero UUID.   * &#x60;invalid_catalog_source&#x60; — 400, the &#x60;RegisterCatalogSource&#x60; body breached an aggregate invariant (malformed name or status).   * &#x60;invalid_oci_reference&#x60; — 400, the &#x60;RegisterCatalogSource&#x60; &#x60;oci_reference&#x60; was malformed (bad registry/repository, or not exactly one of tag/digest).   * &#x60;invalid_verification_policy&#x60; — 400, the &#x60;RegisterCatalogSource&#x60; &#x60;verification&#x60; policy was malformed.   * &#x60;invalid_tracking_policy&#x60; — 400, the &#x60;RegisterCatalogSource&#x60; &#x60;tracking&#x60; policy was malformed (e.g. &#x60;track-tag&#x60; over a digest-pinned reference).   * &#x60;invalid_credential_ref&#x60; — 400, the &#x60;RegisterCatalogSource&#x60; &#x60;credential_ref&#x60; was not a valid &#x60;namespace/name&#x60;.   * &#x60;invalid_import_request&#x60; — 400, the &#x60;ImportFromCatalogSource&#x60; body set neither, both, or an empty &#x60;slugs&#x60;/&#x60;all&#x60;.   * &#x60;catalog_source_not_found&#x60; — 404, the addressed catalog source does not exist.   * &#x60;catalog_artifact_not_found&#x60; — 404, the source&#39;s upstream OCI artifact (or a browsed slug) does not resolve.   * &#x60;catalog_upstream_error&#x60; — 502, the upstream registry was unreachable or returned a malformed bundle on browse or an &#x60;all&#x60; import listing.   * &#x60;blueprint_catalogs_not_provisioned&#x60; — 501, the composition root has not wired the Blueprint catalog-source dependency bundle yet.  The Blueprint catalog-source surface REUSES the shared &#x60;invalid_body&#x60;, &#x60;request_body_too_large&#x60;, &#x60;unauthenticated&#x60;, &#x60;permission_denied&#x60;, and &#x60;internal&#x60; codes with the same semantics they carry on the surfaces above.  The Tenancy Resource surface adds the closed taxonomy below. Each code maps to exactly one repo / service sentinel and one HTTP status:    * &#x60;invalid_resource_origin&#x60; — 400, &#x60;CreateResource&#x60; body &#x60;origin&#x60; was absent or not one of &#x60;adopted&#x60; / &#x60;provisioned&#x60;.   * &#x60;invalid_resource_id&#x60; — 400, path &#x60;{id}&#x60; on &#x60;/v1/resources/{id}&#x60; was not a non-zero UUID.   * &#x60;blueprint_provider_mismatch&#x60; — 422, the &#x60;CreateResource&#x60; provisioned flow named a Blueprint version whose accepted provider kinds do not include the provider of the Cloud behind the named credential. Refused before the ProvisionedResource is minted.   * &#x60;resource_not_found&#x60; — 404, the addressed Resource does not exist or is not visible.   * &#x60;resources_not_provisioned&#x60; — 501, the composition root has not wired the Resource dependency bundle yet.  The Tenancy Resource surface REUSES the shared &#x60;invalid_project_id&#x60;, &#x60;project_not_found&#x60;, &#x60;invalid_body&#x60;, &#x60;invalid_limit&#x60;, &#x60;invalid_cursor&#x60;, &#x60;cursor_binding_mismatch&#x60;, &#x60;request_body_too_large&#x60;, &#x60;unauthenticated&#x60;, and &#x60;internal&#x60; codes with the same semantics they carry on the Cloud Inventory and Tenancy surfaces above.  The Bridge Orchestrator surface adds the closed taxonomy below. Each code maps to exactly one repo / service / domain sentinel and one HTTP status:    * &#x60;resource_not_bridge&#x60; — 409, the addressed Resource exists but is not of kind &#x60;bridge&#x60;; emitted by every mutating bridge operation before any persistence write.   * &#x60;port_out_of_range&#x60; — 400, a &#x60;listen_port&#x60; (relay, user-access provider) or &#x60;remote_port&#x60; (site-to-site tunnel) was outside the closed range &#x60;1..65535&#x60;.   * &#x60;slug_conflict&#x60; — 409, a many-aggregate create or patch collided on &#x60;(resource_id, slug)&#x60; (user-access, ingress, site-to-site) or on &#x60;(resource_id, sni_host)&#x60; (ingress).   * &#x60;target_node_not_in_domain&#x60; — 400, an ingress rule&#39;s &#x60;target_node_id&#x60; resolves to a Node outside the bridge Resource&#39;s owning Domain.   * &#x60;allowed_subnet_empty&#x60; — 400, a site-to-site tunnel create or patch supplied an empty &#x60;allowed_subnets&#x60; list.   * &#x60;secret_ref_malformed&#x60; — 400, an &#x60;auth_secret_ref&#x60; (user-access, site-to-site) did not match the opaque &#x60;secret:&lt;domain&gt;/&lt;project&gt;/&lt;name&gt;(:&lt;version&gt;)?&#x60; form.  The Bridge Orchestrator surface REUSES the shared &#x60;invalid_project_id&#x60;, &#x60;project_not_found&#x60;, &#x60;invalid_resource_id&#x60;, &#x60;resource_not_found&#x60;, &#x60;invalid_body&#x60;, &#x60;request_body_too_large&#x60;, &#x60;permission_denied&#x60;, &#x60;unauthenticated&#x60;, and &#x60;internal&#x60; codes with the same semantics they carry on the Tenancy Resource surface above.  The tenant sink, sink-enablement, and Telemetry Route surface adds the closed taxonomy below. Each code maps to exactly one domain / repo / service sentinel and one HTTP status:    * &#x60;sink_invalid&#x60; — 422, the Sink aggregate refused the body: a malformed slug, an oversized display name, a type no tenant may declare, an endpoint invalid for the stated type or naming a literal address inside the platform&#39;s own network, a CA bundle holding no certificate, or a dataset on a type other than &#x60;otlp&#x60;.   * &#x60;sink_not_found&#x60; — 404, the addressed sink does not exist, or a body named a sink that does not.   * &#x60;sink_slug_taken&#x60; — 409, a create or replace would take a slug another sink already holds in the same scope.   * &#x60;sink_conflict&#x60; — 409, a write cannot be applied against the stored sink for a reason other than the slug: it would move the sink to another Domain or flip its built-in discriminator, or it addresses a built-in sink, which is platform-provided and neither updatable nor deletable.   * &#x60;sink_cas_conflict&#x60; — 409, &#x60;UpdateSink&#x60;&#39;s &#x60;expected_updated_at&#x60; did not match the stored sink&#39;s &#x60;updated_at&#x60;. The body is the full post-image, so applying a stale one would silently restore every mutable field the writer never looked at.   * &#x60;sink_limit_reached&#x60; — 409, the Domain already holds the maximum number of tenant sinks. The Domain listing is unpaginated and every route picks its targets from the same roster, so the ceiling is what keeps both bounded.   * &#x60;sinks_not_provisioned&#x60; — 501, the composition root has not wired the sink dependency bundle yet.   * &#x60;sink_enablement_not_found&#x60; — 404, the addressed sink enablement does not exist.   * &#x60;duplicate_live_sink_enablement&#x60; — 409, a live (requested or approved) enablement already exists for the same (Project, sink) pair.   * &#x60;sink_not_enableable&#x60; — 422, the named sink is built in; a built-in sink is reachable from a route without a grant, so there is nothing to enable.   * &#x60;sink_domain_mismatch&#x60; — 422, the sink and the Project belong to different Domains, so the grant would cross a tenancy boundary.   * &#x60;revocation_sync_pending&#x60; — 502, a revocation committed but the &#x60;uses&#x60; edge delete did not complete, so the Project still holds the grant and keeps delivering. Reported as a failure rather than as a completed revocation because the direction is fail-open; a retry is refused (&#x60;revoked&#x60; is terminal) and the removal is left to the committed event replaying through the authz-sync arm.   * &#x60;sink_enablements_not_provisioned&#x60; — 501, the composition root has not wired the sink-enablement dependency bundle yet.   * &#x60;telemetry_route_invalid&#x60; — 422, the Route aggregate refused the body: an unknown signal, a severity floor on a non-&#x60;logs&#x60; route, a name prefix on a non-&#x60;metrics&#x60; route, an oversized prefix, an empty &#x60;sink_ids&#x60;, more than sixteen sink ids, a zero sink id, or a sink named twice.   * &#x60;telemetry_route_not_found&#x60; — 404, the addressed Telemetry Route does not exist.   * &#x60;route_sink_not_found&#x60; — 422, a &#x60;sink_ids&#x60; entry names no sink.   * &#x60;route_sink_not_usable&#x60; — 422, a &#x60;sink_ids&#x60; entry names a tenant sink the Project holds no live approved enablement for, so the route would deliver nowhere.   * &#x60;route_signal_not_accepted&#x60; — 422, a target sink&#39;s type cannot receive the route&#39;s signal — a metrics route to a log backend, say — so the route would only ever go dark.   * &#x60;route_project_mismatch&#x60; — 422, a stated post-image names a different Project than the stored route belongs to; the persisted &#x60;project_id&#x60; is immutable.   * &#x60;route_limit_reached&#x60; — 409, the Project already holds the maximum number of routes. The delivery engine walks a Project&#39;s routes for every buffered batch, so the ceiling is what keeps that walk bounded.   * &#x60;telemetry_routes_not_provisioned&#x60; — 501, the composition root has not wired the Telemetry Route dependency bundle yet.  The surface REUSES the shared &#x60;domain_not_found&#x60;, &#x60;project_not_found&#x60;, &#x60;illegal_transition&#x60;, &#x60;invalid_body&#x60;, &#x60;invalid_limit&#x60;, &#x60;invalid_cursor&#x60;, &#x60;cursor_binding_mismatch&#x60;, &#x60;invalid_decision_reason&#x60;, &#x60;permission_denied&#x60;, &#x60;unauthenticated&#x60;, and &#x60;internal&#x60; codes with the same semantics they carry on the surfaces above.  Dependency-degradation codes are global rather than scoped to a single surface: any operation can return &#x60;503&#x60; when a dependency it needs is briefly unavailable, instead of a generic &#x60;5xx&#x60;, so a client branches on &#x60;code&#x60; to back off, fail over, or page rather than string-matching opaque internal errors. Each code maps to one dependency outage and one HTTP status; the operator runbook is &#x60;docs/operations/failure-modes.md&#x60;:    * &#x60;authz_unavailable&#x60; — 503, the ReBAC backend (SpiceDB) is     unreachable so an authorization decision could not be     reached. Emitted GLOBALLY by every ReBAC-gated operation —     no handler fails open. Within the per-Domain stale-check     TTL a last-known-good allow/deny may be served instead     (recorded under a distinct audit reason); past the TTL, or     for a subject not in the stale cache, the operation     returns this code.   * &#x60;event_stream_unavailable&#x60; — 503, &#x60;GetNodeEvents&#x60; could     not open the signed event stream because the message bus     (NATS JetStream) is unreachable. The reconciliation-pull     &#x60;GetNodeState&#x60; path does not depend on the message bus and     stays available during the same outage.   * &#x60;datastore_unavailable&#x60; — 503, &#x60;GetNodeState&#x60; could not     serve a snapshot because the datastore (Postgres) is     unreachable AND no fresh-enough cached snapshot exists for     the addressed Node. A Node with a fresh-enough cached     snapshot is still served &#x60;200&#x60; during the same outage.   * &#x60;signing_unavailable&#x60; — 503, &#x60;IssueSession&#x60; could not mint     a session token because the Signing Service is     unreachable. No Session is persisted and no token issued,     so a retry after recovery is safe.   * &#x60;openbao_unavailable&#x60; — 503, a node-secret read could not     complete because the secret backend (OpenBao) is sealed or     unreachable. DIVERGENCE NOTE: the project README&#39;s     degradation table uses the illustrative string     &#x60;secret_backend_unavailable&#x60; for this case, but the     shipped wire code is &#x60;openbao_unavailable&#x60;. The wire code     is authoritative — renaming it would be a breaking change     for zero behavioural gain — so the divergence is     documented here rather than reconciled.  None of the dependency-degradation codes carry the underlying error text on the wire: the cause is logged in the server&#39;s structured record only, and the Problem &#x60;detail&#x60; is a fixed, generic, retry-oriented string.  | [optional] 
**dimension** | **str** | Optional capacity-and-scale axis this problem concerns. Set EXCLUSIVELY by the &#x60;capacity_exceeded&#x60; refusals — the per-Domain observability-ingest byte ceiling (&#x60;observability_ingest&#x60;) and the per-Domain concurrent action-execution ceiling (&#x60;action_executions&#x60;) — so a client can attribute the throttle to a specific scale axis without string-matching &#x60;detail&#x60;. The value is one of the &#x60;CapacityDimension&#x60; members; other problem instances omit the field.  | [optional] 
**child_counts** | [**DomainChildCounts**](DomainChildCounts.md) | Optional structured payload set EXCLUSIVELY by the &#x60;domain_not_empty&#x60; problem (&#x60;DELETE /v1/domains/{id}&#x60; blocked by remaining child aggregates). Other problem instances omit the field. The generated client should treat its presence as a strong signal the response code is &#x60;domain_not_empty&#x60;.  | [optional] 
**project_child_counts** | [**ProjectChildCounts**](ProjectChildCounts.md) | Optional structured payload set EXCLUSIVELY by the &#x60;project_not_empty&#x60; problem (&#x60;DELETE /v1/projects/{id}&#x60; blocked by remaining child aggregates). Other problem instances omit the field. The generated client should treat its presence as a strong signal the response code is &#x60;project_not_empty&#x60;.  | [optional] 
**cloud_child_counts** | [**CloudChildCounts**](CloudChildCounts.md) | Optional structured payload set EXCLUSIVELY by the &#x60;cloud_not_empty&#x60; problem (&#x60;DELETE /v1/clouds/{id}&#x60; blocked by remaining child aggregates). Other problem instances omit the field. The generated client should treat its presence as a strong signal the response code is &#x60;cloud_not_empty&#x60;.  | [optional] 
**referencing_clouds** | **int** | Optional count set EXCLUSIVELY by the &#x60;provider_bundle_referenced&#x60; problem (&#x60;DELETE /v1/provider-bundles/{id}&#x60; blocked by Clouds that still take their provider configuration from the bundle). It states how many Clouds reference the bundle, so the operator knows the size of the re-pointing job before retrying. The field is absent on the racing arm, where a Cloud starts referencing the bundle between the guard&#39;s count and the DELETE and the foreign-key violation reaches the same code without a count.  | [optional]
